title: Year With the Most People Alive
statement:
You get a list logs where logs[i] = [birth, death] are the birth and death years of one person. That person counts as alive in every year from birth up to death − 1. The death year itself does not count.

Return the year in which the most people were alive. If several years tie, return the earliest one.

examples.why: Both people are alive from 1970 through 1974. 1970 is the first of those years.
In 2000 the first person has already died, so no year has two people. Every year from 1990 has one, and 1990 is the earliest.
1960 has three people alive (the first one dies in 1961). 1962 also has three, but 1960 comes first.

hints: There are only about a hundred possible years. Counting people for every year directly is already fast enough here.
A neater way: a birth adds one person from that year on, and a death removes one from that year on. Record +1 at birth and −1 at death.
Walk the years in order with a running total of those changes. The first year where the running total reaches a new maximum is the answer.

explain.intuition:
Instead of asking "who is alive in year y?" for every year, note what changes from one year to the next. The population goes up by one at each birth year and down by one at each death year. Record those changes in a small array indexed by year, then a running sum turns the changes back into the population of every year. This is the difference-array trick, the same idea as counting how many events overlap a time slot in a calendar.

Because the death year gets its −1 in that year, a person born in 2000 does not overlap a person who died in 2000, exactly as the rule says. Taking only a strictly larger running total as a new best gives the earliest year on ties.
steps: Create delta with one slot per year from 1950 to 2050.
Walk the years in order, keeping alive += delta[year].
When alive is strictly greater than the best so far, store it and the year.
pitfalls: Counting the death year as alive. In [[1990, 2000], [2000, 2010]] that wrongly makes 2000 the busiest year.
Using ≥ when updating the best, which returns the latest tied year instead of the earliest.
Making the array one slot short. A death in 2050 writes to index 2050 − 1950 = 100, so you need 101 slots.

complexity.time: O(n + Y), Y = number of years

solutions.title: Count every year directly
solutions.idea: For each year, count the people with birth ≤ year < death. Keep the first year with the highest count.

solutions.title: Difference array over the years
solutions.idea: +1 at each birth, −1 at each death, then a running sum gives the population of every year in one pass.

followups: Years can now be any integer up to 10⁹. How do you avoid a giant array? (Hint: sort the events.)
Return every maximal stretch of years at the peak population, not just the first year.
